newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T H1 focus will be on U.S. litigation.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T H1 focus will be on U.S. litigation.

text.p: British tobacco-to-insurance group B.A.T Industries is expected to report lower first-half profits on July 30 as sterling's strength and competitive U.S. tobacco markets take their toll, analysts said.

But the one burning issue for the company remains current litigation against cigarette producers in the U.S., where a $368 billion proposed settlement deal, which B.A.T has said would cost its U.S. unit Brown and Williamson $1.7 billion, still awaits the approval of Congress.
Under the agreement, the tobacco industry has accepted tougher regulation on both products and advertising in return for immunity from big legal claims over the impact of smoking on health.
Individual claims can still be brought, albeit under significant restrictions including no claims for punitive damages.

"Progress towards a settlement in the U.S. is crucial, there could still be some nasty moments to come and there could be a significant impact on profitability," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.

Pretax profits for the six months are expected to be between 1.237 and 1.301 billion stg, down from 1.331 billion previously, with a dividend payout of around 10.7-10.8 pence per share, up from 10 pence.
Price competition in U.S. markets and the recent strength of the pound on foreign exchange markets are likely to have hit profits, analysts said.
"Price competition in U.S. markets could bring in poor figures there," said the analyst.
In Europe, analysts expect a mixed result on the group's tobacco business, while Latin America, Africa and Australia could show growth in sales.
B.A.T bought Mexico's largest cigarette maker Cigarerra La Moderna for $1.7 billion earlier this month in a move aimed at sealing its dominance of the area's lucrative market.
The company's insurance business will also be eyed for signs of improvement, analysts said.
But they said that a demerger of the operations, widely rumoured to be a possibility earlier this year, was unlikely to be on the agenda.
"The possibility of a tobacco settlement puts all demerger talk on the back burner. That's the only issue for B.A.T at the moment," the analyst said. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
